title: State elimination for mixed‐integer optimal control of partial differential equations by semigroup theory
contribution: A one-time state-elimination reformulation for MIPDECOs whose PDE has abstract-ODE (semigroup) structure, avoiding repeated state computations for all time steps (abstract).
problem_entry: MIPDECOs are powerful but challenging in theory and computation; target time-dependent PDEs with abstract-ODE structure in function space (abstract).
key_idea: Use semigroup theory to eliminate the states once before optimization, so states are not recomputed for every time step (abstract).
assumptions: PDE has the structure of an abstract ordinary differential equation in function space (abstract).
experiments: Numerical experiments complement the theory (abstract); details not read.
limits_future: Not stated in the abstract (not read).

method_links.note: MIPDECO as an extension class; reformulation to make it tractable for mixed-integer methods

transferable: When the PDE is an abstract ODE in function space, precompute the solution operator once and substitute it for the states so the mixed-integer problem is posed in the controls only (abstract).

quotes.text: We propose a highly efficient state elimination approach for MIPDECOs that are governed by partial differential equations that have the structure of an abstract ordinary differential equation in function space.
This allows us to avoid repeated calculations of the states for all time steps, and our approach is applied only once before starting the optimization.

title: A Bilevel Optimization Framework for Dynamically Correcting Imbalance in Two-class Classification Problems
contribution: A bilevel framework that, after training the model parameters, optimizes over majority-class samples and keeps only those that improve the loss, for imbalanced two-class classification (abstract).
problem_entry: Indiscriminate oversampling ignores how added samples affect classification, which hurts accuracy under noise and causes underfitting (abstract).
key_idea: Upper level selects majority-class training samples, lower level is the usual model-parameter training; accept only samples that improve the loss (abstract).
experiments: F1 scores up to 10% higher than state-of-the-art methods (abstract); data sets and baselines not read.
positioning: Positioned against data rebalancing by undersampling/oversampling (abstract).
limits_future: Not stated in the abstract (not read).

method_links.note: ML data-selection problem re-cast as bilevel optimization
abstract gives an 'up to 10%' F1 gain over unnamed baselines without a fairness statement; paper body not read; student first author

quotes.text: Our framework allows us to dynamically assess a sample’s impact on loss and accepts only those datapoints that improve loss, thereby, finding an optimal subset of majority training data for classification.
Experimental results show our proposed technique with F1 scores up to 10% higher than state-of-the-art methods.

title: maestro
contribution: MÆSTRO, a derivative-free stochastic trust-region solver that fits noisy Monte Carlo simulations to experimental data by modelling signal and noise locally in each trust region (abstract).
problem_entry: Least-squares calibration of resource-intensive, noisy Monte Carlo simulations to noisy experimental data (abstract).
key_idea: Each iteration: run simulations at design points in the trust region, build local approximations of signal and noise, solve the closed-form subproblem, move the trust region (abstract).
assumptions: Noisy, expensive simulation; least-squares objective; no derivatives (abstract).

method_links.note: trust-region toolkit carried into stochastic simulation calibration
method released as a stand-alone solver (DOE software record)

transferable: For a noisy simulator, fit local models of both the signal and the noise at trust-region design points and solve the surrogate subproblem in closed form (abstract).
coauthors: M. Krishnamoorthy, T. Peterka, O. Yildiz, S. Mrenna

quotes.text: This problem is solved using a stochastic trust-region optimization algorithm where in each iteration, a local approximation of the simulation signal and of the simulation noise is constructed over data, which is obtained by running the simulation at strategically placed design points within the trust-region around the current iterate.
